newsitem.title: USA: Fire destroys Indiana basketball star's home.
newsitem.headline: Fire destroys Indiana basketball star's home.

text.p: A fire Thursday destroyed Indiana Pacers basketball star Reggie Miller's home and possessions valued at $2.5 million, authorities said.
"There were only a couple of walls left standing," fire department Lt. Chad Abel said.

The 14,000 square foot home, built in the late 1980s, was undergoing renovations and was unoccupied, but hundreds of thousands of dollars worth of rugs, furniture and clothing were lost. The cause of the early morning fire was not known.
Although the three-story home was surrounded on three sides by a reservoir, firefighters were hampered by the absence of a hydrant nearby, Hamilton County Sheriff's spokesman Eddie Moore said.

Miller, the sharp-shooting perennial NBA All-Star and a member of U.S. Olympic "Dream Team," was visibly shaken when he arrived and saw his house consumed by the blaze, authorities said. Several friends from the Pacers team arrived to lend support.
Fishers is town of 25,000 just outside Indianapolis with several wealthy housing subdivisions.
